# 12-Week Strength Programme: Post-Meniscectomy Return to Skiing

**Client snapshot:** 36-year-old recreational lifter, 6 months post right medial meniscus repair, cleared for low-impact strength training. Restrictions: no jumping/impact, no deep knee flexion under load (keep loaded knee flexion ≤ ~90°). Goal: rebuild strength base, then drive ski-specific qualities — quad/glute/posterior chain strength, single-leg stability, isometric endurance, frontal/transverse plane control, and trunk robustness.

**Structure:** Four 4-week phases (the last is a 1-week transition), 4 sessions/week. Phase 1 builds capacity and corrects asymmetry; Phase 2 builds general strength; Phase 3 emphasises ski-specific strength and unilateral work; Phase 4 peaks and tapers into a return-to-snow protocol.

**General rules across the block:**
- Box squat / leg press depth capped where knee flexion stays ≤ ~90° throughout.
- No barbell back squats below parallel, no jumping/landing, no high-rep loaded step-downs early on.
- RPE-driven loading. Add load when reps are clean and RPE is 1 below target.
- Warm-up every session: 5 min bike, ankle mobility, hip airplanes, glute bridges, terminal knee extensions (TKE) with band, 2-min couch stretch.
- Track right vs left single-leg metrics weekly (leg press, split squat hold). Target: <10% asymmetry by week 8.

---

## PHASE 1 — Reconditioning & Symmetry (Weeks 1–4)

Goal: build tissue tolerance, re-pattern squat and hinge, restore single-leg control. Volume moderate, intensity low (RPE 6–7). Sets x reps shown; rest 90 sec accessories, 2 min compounds.

**Weekly split:**
- Day 1: Lower (bilateral focus)
- Day 2: Upper push + core
- Day 3: Lower (unilateral focus)
- Day 4: Upper pull + posterior chain

### Day 1 — Lower bilateral
- Goblet box squat (box at parallel, knee ~90°): 4 x 8
- Leg press (limited ROM, knee ~90° max): 3 x 10
- Romanian deadlift: 3 x 8
- Standing calf raise: 3 x 12
- TKE with band: 3 x 15 each
- Side plank: 3 x 30 sec each

### Day 2 — Upper push + core
- Dumbbell bench press: 4 x 8
- Standing DB overhead press: 3 x 10
- Cable chest fly: 3 x 12
- Triceps rope pushdown: 3 x 12
- Dead bug: 3 x 10 each
- Pallof press: 3 x 10 each

### Day 3 — Lower unilateral
- Rear-foot elevated split squat (front foot well forward, shallow ROM): 3 x 8 each
- Step-up to low box (~ knee-height max, ~90° flexion): 3 x 8 each
- Single-leg leg press: 3 x 10 each
- Copenhagen plank (short lever): 3 x 20 sec each
- Hamstring curl (lying or seated): 3 x 12

### Day 4 — Upper pull + posterior
- Chest-supported row: 4 x 8
- Lat pulldown: 3 x 10
- Hip thrust (barbell, controlled): 4 x 10
- 45° back extension: 3 x 12
- Face pull: 3 x 15
- Suitcase carry: 3 x 30 sec each

**Week-by-week:**
- **Week 1:** All sets at RPE 6. Emphasise tempo (3-1-1) on squats and split squats.
- **Week 2:** Add one set to leg press and RDL. RPE 6–7.
- **Week 3:** Increase load 2.5–5% on compounds where week 2 RPE was ≤ 7. Introduce 2-second pause at bottom of split squat.
- **Week 4 (deload):** Drop volume 30% across the board, keep loads. Reassess single-leg symmetry, knee swelling, soreness pattern before progressing.

---

## PHASE 2 — General Strength (Weeks 5–8)

Goal: build a strength base in the 5–8 rep range with bilateral and unilateral lifts. ROM expanded if symptom-free, but back squat depth still capped at parallel and split squats stay shallow. Intensity RPE 7–8.

**Weekly split:** Lower / Upper / Lower / Upper, same structure as Phase 1.

### Day 1 — Lower bilateral (strength)
- Safety bar box squat to parallel: 5 x 5
- Trap bar deadlift (low handles, controlled): 4 x 6
- Leg press: 3 x 8
- Standing calf raise: 4 x 8
- Hanging knee raise: 3 x 10

### Day 2 — Upper push
- Barbell bench press: 5 x 5
- Standing overhead press: 4 x 6
- Incline DB press: 3 x 8
- Cable triceps extension: 3 x 10
- Pallof press: 3 x 10 each

### Day 3 — Lower unilateral (strength)
- Rear-foot elevated split squat (DBs): 4 x 6 each
- Reverse lunge to low box: 3 x 8 each
- Single-leg RDL: 3 x 8 each
- Nordic hamstring eccentric (assisted): 3 x 5
- Copenhagen plank: 3 x 25 sec each

### Day 4 — Upper pull + posterior
- Weighted chin-up or assisted: 4 x 6
- Pendlay or chest-supported row: 4 x 8
- Hip thrust: 4 x 6
- 45° back extension (weighted): 3 x 10
- Farmer carry: 3 x 40 m

**Week-by-week:**
- **Week 5:** Establish working loads at RPE 7. Film split squat — check valgus on right knee.
- **Week 6:** Add 2.5–5 kg to squat/deadlift, small jumps on accessories. RPE 7.5.
- **Week 7:** Peak week of phase. Top sets of squat and bench at RPE 8. Begin testing single-leg leg press 5RM each side to track symmetry.
- **Week 8 (deload):** Volume −40%, intensity held. Reassess. Decision point: if right-leg single-leg leg press is within 10% of left, progress to ski-specific phase loaded. If not, repeat week 6 before advancing.

---

## PHASE 3 — Ski-Specific Strength (Weeks 9–11)

Goal: bias the qualities skiing demands — eccentric quad strength, isometric endurance (the "ski sit"), lateral hip strength, trunk anti-rotation, and unilateral force production. No impact yet; this is loaded prep, not on-snow simulation.

**Weekly split:**
- Day 1: Lower — strength + ski isometrics
- Day 2: Upper push + rotational core
- Day 3: Lower — unilateral + lateral
- Day 4: Upper pull + posterior chain

### Day 1 — Lower strength + isometrics
- Safety bar box squat: 4 x 5 @ RPE 8
- Tempo leg press (4-second eccentric, ~90° max): 4 x 6
- Wall sit at ski-relevant angle (~knees 100–110°): 4 x 30–45 sec
- Romanian deadlift: 3 x 6
- Standing calf raise: 4 x 8
- Pallof iso-hold: 3 x 20 sec each

### Day 2 — Upper push + rotational core
- Bench press: 4 x 5
- Landmine press: 3 x 8 each
- Incline DB press: 3 x 8
- Cable woodchop: 3 x 10 each
- Side plank with reach: 3 x 10 each

### Day 3 — Lower unilateral + lateral
- Rear-foot elevated split squat (eccentric tempo 3-1-1): 4 x 6 each
- Lateral step-up to low box: 3 x 8 each
- Skater squat (assisted, partial ROM): 3 x 6 each
- Cable hip abduction (standing): 3 x 12 each
- Copenhagen plank (long lever if tolerated): 3 x 30 sec each
- Single-leg calf raise: 3 x 10 each

### Day 4 — Upper pull + posterior
- Weighted chin-up: 4 x 5
- Barbell or chest-supported row: 4 x 6
- Hip thrust: 4 x 5 heavy
- Single-leg hip thrust: 3 x 8 each
- 45° back extension: 3 x 10
- Suitcase carry: 3 x 40 m each side

**Week-by-week:**
- **Week 9:** Introduce tempo eccentrics and wall sits. Keep load moderate while the new stimulus settles.
- **Week 10:** Push wall sit duration to 60 sec; add load to split squat. Begin a single weekly bike interval session (8 x 30 sec hard / 90 sec easy) — non-impact ski conditioning.
- **Week 11:** Heaviest week. Top sets of box squat, bench, chin-up at RPE 8.5. Final symmetry test: single-leg leg press, split squat 5RM, single-leg calf raise reps. Target <5% asymmetry.

---

## PHASE 4 — Taper & Transition (Week 12)

Goal: reduce fatigue, retain strength, transition to on-snow readiness. Volume −50%, intensity held on main lifts at RPE 7. Three sessions only.

### Day 1 — Lower
- Box squat: 3 x 3 @ RPE 7
- Split squat: 3 x 5 each
- Wall sit: 3 x 45 sec
- TKE: 2 x 15

### Day 2 — Upper full body
- Bench press: 3 x 3
- Chin-up: 3 x 3
- Hip thrust: 3 x 5
- Pallof press: 2 x 10 each

### Day 3 — Lower light + skiing prep
- Leg press: 3 x 5 light
- Lateral step-up: 2 x 8 each
- Single-leg RDL: 2 x 6 each
- Copenhagen plank: 2 x 20 sec each
- Bike: 20 min easy

---

## Recovery, monitoring, and return-to-snow notes

- **Knee monitoring:** Track morning effusion (visual + 1-finger sweep test), pain (0–10) before and after each lower session, and soreness 24 hr later. Any increase in swelling that lasts >24 hr = repeat previous week.
- **Sleep & soft tissue:** Aim 7–8 hr sleep. Foam roll quads, adductors, calves daily; couch stretch 2 min/side daily.
- **Conditioning:** Bike or rower only through Phase 1–2. Add the bike intervals in Phase 3 (week 10 onward). No running, no jumping, no plyometrics in this 12-week block.
- **Return-to-snow checklist** (post-Phase 4, before he books a trip): symmetry <10% on single-leg leg press, 60 sec wall sit pain-free, single-leg RDL with bodyweight + 20 kg clean, no effusion after lower sessions for 4 consecutive weeks. If all green, the next block (weeks 13–16) introduces low-amplitude landing mechanics, lateral bounds, and ski-specific reactive work — not before.

Let me know his current numbers on squat, deadlift, bench and single-leg leg press and I'll plug in starting loads for week 1.

# Nutrition Plan: 12-Week Strength Block, Weight Maintenance

To dial this in properly I'd want his bodyweight, height, body-fat estimate, and job activity level. Without those, I'll build the framework around a typical 36-year-old recreational lifter and give you the formulas to plug his actual numbers in. I'll assume **82 kg, ~18% body fat, desk job with 4 gym sessions/week** as the worked example — adjust from there.

---

## Calorie target

**Method:** Mifflin-St Jeor × activity multiplier.

- BMR (male) = 10 × kg + 6.25 × cm − 5 × age + 5
- Worked example (82 kg, 180 cm, 36): BMR ≈ 1,770 kcal
- Activity multiplier for desk job + 4 lifting sessions: **1.5**
- TDEE ≈ **2,650 kcal/day** for maintenance

Adjust ±100 kcal after 2 weeks based on scale trend (weekly average, not daily).

**Maintenance target: 2,650 kcal/day** (example).

---

## Macros

Rebuilding around a knee injury and strength training both push protein needs up. Carbs stay high to fuel lifting; fat covers the rest.

| Macro | g/kg | Example (82 kg) | kcal | % of total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Protein | 2.0 | 165 g | 660 | 25% |
| Carbs | 4.5 | 370 g | 1,480 | 56% |
| Fat | 0.7 | 60 g | 540 | 20% |
| **Total** | | | **~2,680** | |

**Why these numbers:**
- **Protein 2.0 g/kg:** upper end of the strength-training range and supports connective tissue remodelling post-meniscectomy. Spread across 4 meals (~40 g each) to maximise muscle protein synthesis.
- **Carbs 4.5 g/kg:** supports training volume in Phases 2–3 without surplus. Bias toward training windows.
- **Fat 0.7 g/kg:** floor for hormonal health, not a ceiling. Fill remaining calories.

---

## Meal structure (training day example)

**Breakfast (~600 kcal):** 4 whole eggs, 80 g oats, 1 banana, black coffee. ~40 g P / 70 g C / 22 g F.

**Lunch (~700 kcal):** 180 g grilled chicken, 200 g cooked rice, large mixed salad with 1 tbsp olive oil, vegetables. ~50 g P / 85 g C / 15 g F.

**Pre-training snack (~300 kcal, 60–90 min before):** Greek yogurt 200 g + 50 g granola + berries. ~25 g P / 50 g C / 5 g F.

**Post-training / dinner (~750 kcal):** 200 g salmon or lean beef, 300 g potatoes, 200 g roasted veg. ~50 g P / 80 g C / 25 g F.

**Evening (~300 kcal):** Cottage cheese 200 g + handful almonds + apple. ~30 g P / 25 g C / 12 g F.

**Daily total:** ~2,650 kcal, 195 g P / 310 g C / 79 g F. Protein lands a bit above target — fine, drop a yogurt portion or swap to mixed if you want it tighter on macros.

**Rest day adjustment:** Drop carbs by ~80 g (roughly: skip pre-training snack, halve the rice at lunch). Keeps protein and fat steady, brings total to ~2,300 kcal. Over the week this averages near maintenance.

---

## Nutrient timing

- **Protein:** 35–45 g every 3–4 hours, four feedings. One within ~2 hours post-lift.
- **Carbs:** majority in the meals around training (lunch if he trains evening, pre/post snack if he trains midday).
- **Pre-lift:** 30–50 g carbs + 20–30 g protein, 60–90 min out. Easily digested.
- **Post-lift:** Full meal within 2 hours. No need for a separate shake if a meal is coming.
- **Before bed:** Casein-rich food (cottage cheese, Greek yogurt) supports overnight recovery and connective tissue turnover.

---

## Supplements (evidence-supported, optional)

- **Creatine monohydrate:** 5 g/day, any time. Strength and lean mass benefit; safe long-term.
- **Whey protein:** 1 scoop as needed to hit daily protein target. Convenience, not magic.
- **Vitamin D3:** 1,000–2,000 IU/day, especially through winter. Worth testing serum 25(OH)D if he hasn't.
- **Omega-3 (EPA+DHA):** 2 g/day combined. Useful through the injury recovery window for tissue health.
- **Collagen + vitamin C:** 15 g hydrolysed collagen + 50 mg vitamin C, 30–60 min pre-training. Some evidence for connective tissue and tendon/ligament adaptation — relevant post-meniscectomy. Worth running through this 12-week block.
- **Caffeine:** 3–6 mg/kg pre-training if he uses it, capped before mid-afternoon.

Skip: BCAAs (redundant with adequate protein), fat burners, glucosamine/chondroitin (evidence weak for post-meniscectomy outcomes).

---

## Hydration

- **Daily:** ~35 ml/kg = ~2.9 L for the example client. More on hot days or hard sessions.
- **Training:** 500 ml in the 2 hours pre-lift, sips through the session, 500–750 ml post.
- **Alcohol:** Blunts protein synthesis, sleep quality, and tissue healing. Recommend ≤4 drinks/week, none on training day evenings. This matters more than usual given the rehab context.

---

## Monitoring & adjustment

- **Weigh-ins:** Same time, 3–4 mornings/week, take the weekly average.
- **Trend rule:** If weekly average shifts >0.5 kg in either direction for 2 consecutive weeks, adjust calories by ±150 kcal (carbs only — keep protein and fat fixed).
- **Performance check:** Gym lifts should track up through Phases 2–3. If strength stalls and weight is stable, food is likely fine — look at sleep and stress first.
- **Phase-specific cues:**
  - **Phase 1 (weeks 1–4):** Energy demand modest. If he's not hungry, don't force feed — staying right at maintenance is fine.
  - **Phase 2 (weeks 5–8):** Volume climbs. Watch for unintentional drift downward in weight; nudge carbs up 30–50 g/day if needed.
  - **Phase 3 (weeks 9–11):** Hardest training and bike intervals start week 10. This is the most likely spot for under-fuelling. Keep an eye on session quality and recovery markers.
  - **Phase 4 (week 12):** Taper. Drop ~150 kcal (carbs) since training volume is halved.

---

## Practical handouts to give him

1. **A daily protein target in grams** (sticky-note on the fridge).
2. **A "default plate" rule** for unplanned meals: palm of protein, fist of carbs, thumb of fat, two fists of veg.
3. **A pre/post training meal he can rotate** so decisions are automatic on gym days.
4. **A "non-negotiables" list:** hit protein, train fed, sleep 7+ hr, hydrate, limit alcohol.

Once you send me his actual bodyweight, height, and a sense of his job activity, I'll re-run the numbers and give you his specific calorie and macro targets to hand over.

# Adding Cardio: 2 Sessions/Week

Two cardio sessions slot in cleanly without compromising the strength work, provided we keep them low-impact (no running, no jumping) and use them to support — not sabotage — the lower-body lifting. Here's how I'd structure them across the 12 weeks.

---

## Weekly placement

Original split was Lower / Upper / Lower / Upper across 4 days. Add cardio on **two non-consecutive days that aren't the day before a lower session**.

**Revised weekly layout:**
- **Mon:** Lower (bilateral)
- **Tue:** Upper push + core
- **Wed:** Cardio session 1
- **Thu:** Lower (unilateral)
- **Fri:** Upper pull + posterior
- **Sat:** Cardio session 2
- **Sun:** Rest

This puts cardio 24+ hours after a lower session and 48 hours before the next, so the knee and quads get a clear recovery window.

**Modality rules across the block:**
- **Allowed:** stationary bike, rower, ski erg (upper-body dominant), incline walking on treadmill (≤10% grade, ≤6 km/h), elliptical, swimming.
- **Avoided:** running, stair sprints, jump rope, any impact work, deep-flexion cycling (drop saddle low → no).
- Set bike saddle high enough that the right knee never exceeds ~90° at the top of the pedal stroke.

---

## Phase-by-phase progression

### Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Aerobic base, blood flow, knee tolerance

Goal: low-intensity steady state to drive recovery, build aerobic base, and increase blood flow through the knee without loading it.

- **Session 1 (Wed):** 30 min bike at Zone 2 (RPE 4–5, can hold conversation, ~65–75% max HR).
- **Session 2 (Sat):** 30 min — choose between rower (steady), incline walk, or swim. Athlete's choice for variety.

**Weekly progression:** Week 1: 30 min. Week 2: 35 min. Week 3: 40 min. Week 4 (deload): back to 25 min.

### Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Extend base, introduce intervals

Goal: build work capacity. Add one interval session, keep one Zone 2.

- **Session 1 (Wed):** 40 min bike Zone 2.
- **Session 2 (Sat):** Bike or rower intervals — **6 x 2 min hard (RPE 7) / 2 min easy**, with 5 min warm-up and 5 min cool-down. ~30 min total.

**Weekly progression:** Week 5: as written. Week 6: bump intervals to 7 rounds. Week 7: 8 rounds. Week 8 (deload): drop to 4 rounds, Zone 2 stays 30 min.

Cue: intervals are **effort-based, not knee-stressful**. If the right knee complains, drop resistance and raise cadence — keep the cardiovascular demand, lose the joint load.

### Phase 3 (Weeks 9–11): Ski-specific conditioning

Goal: build sustained-effort capacity that matches a ski run — repeated 1–3 min bouts of hard work with incomplete recovery. This pairs with the wall sits and tempo work in the lifting programme.

- **Session 1 (Wed):** 45 min Zone 2 bike. Long, steady, easy.
- **Session 2 (Sat):** Ski-mimicking intervals on bike — **8 x 90 sec at RPE 8 / 90 sec easy**, with 5 min warm-up and cool-down. Use higher resistance, moderate cadence (60–70 rpm) to bias the quads.

This replaces the single bike interval session I mentioned in week 10 of the original programme — it's now built into the cardio schedule properly.

**Weekly progression:** Week 9: 8 rounds. Week 10: 9 rounds. Week 11: 10 rounds (peak).

### Phase 4 (Week 12): Taper

- **Session 1 (Wed):** 25 min Zone 2 bike, easy.
- **Session 2 (Sat):** 20 min easy bike or walk. Movement, not stimulus.

---

## Calorie adjustment

Two cardio sessions will burn roughly 250–400 kcal each depending on duration and intensity. For weight maintenance, he needs to eat those calories back — otherwise he'll drift into a deficit over a few weeks.

**Recommended adjustment:** Add **~300 kcal on cardio days only**, as carbs (around 75 g). Easiest way: a larger pre- or post-cardio meal, or a banana + Greek yogurt + honey snack worth ~300 kcal.

Weekly maintenance now averages slightly higher because two days are bumped up. Monitor weekly average bodyweight as before; adjust ±150 kcal if the trend drifts.

**Updated example for the 82 kg client:**
- **Lifting + cardio days (Wed, Sat):** ~2,950 kcal
- **Lifting-only days (Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri):** ~2,650 kcal
- **Rest day (Sun):** ~2,300 kcal
- **Weekly average:** ~2,680 kcal, right at maintenance.

- **No sauna or hard cardio** within 48 hr of the strong day — keeps fluid balance and CNS sharp.
- **Light mobility daily**, nothing aggressive.
- **Thursday evening:** big carb meal, early bed (covered in the nutrition section).

---

## Recovery monitoring dashboard

Have him track these four numbers daily in a notes app or notebook. Takes 60 seconds.

1. **Sleep hours + quality (1–10)**
2. **Resting HR (morning, before getting up)**
3. **Knee score (0–10, where 0 = no symptoms)**
4. **Subjective readiness (1–10)**

**Red flag thresholds — auto-deload that day's session:**
- Resting HR >7 bpm above 7-day baseline for 3+ days
- Knee score ≥3 or any new effusion
- Sleep <6 hr the night before
- Readiness ≤4

"Auto-deload" = drop top sets by one, drop accessories by a set each, or switch a hard cardio session for easy Zone 2. Not skip — modify.

**Green light:** all four in normal range = train as programmed, full intent.

---

## What this looks like on a normal day

Just to make it concrete — here's a Thursday in Phase 3 (unilateral lower day):

- **06:30:** Wake. Knee check, resting HR, log. 5 min morning mobility.
- **07:00:** Breakfast.
- **17:30:** Pre-lift warm-up, 10 min.
- **18:00–19:15:** Lower unilateral session.
- **19:15:** Post-lift cool-down, 8 min.
- **19:45:** Dinner.
- **21:00:** Evening mobility, 10 min, plus 5 min foam roll.
- **22:00:** Wind down, screens off.
- **22:30:** Bed.

About 30 min total of recovery work across the day, plus sleep. Sustainable.

---

## Coach prompts to use with him

Things to ask in check-ins, weekly:

- "How's the knee feeling on a scale of 0–10?"
- "Average sleep this week?"
- "How did the heaviest session feel compared to two weeks ago?"
- "Anything stiff or sore that's new?"
- "How was Sunday's recovery — did you actually do it?"

That last one matters. Recovery is the part clients skip. Build accountability for it the same way you'd build accountability for a missed lift.

**Client:** 36-year-old recreational lifter, 6 months post right medial meniscus repair, surgeon-cleared for low-impact strength training. **Goal:** strength and return to skiing, weight maintenance, feeling strong by Week 12.

**Restrictions throughout:** No jumping or impact. No deep knee flexion under load (knee flexion ≤ ~90° on loaded bilateral lifts). No barbell back squats below parallel. No running. No 1RM testing on squat.

# 12-Week Strength Programme: Post-Meniscectomy Return to Skiing
## Integrated Plan — Training, Cardio, Nutrition, Recovery

**Client:** 36-year-old recreational lifter, 6 months post right medial meniscus repair, surgeon-cleared for low-impact strength training. **Goal:** strength and return to skiing, weight maintenance, feeling strong by Week 12.

**Restrictions throughout:** No jumping or impact. No deep knee flexion under load (knee flexion ≤ ~90° on loaded bilateral lifts). No barbell back squats below parallel. No running. No 1RM testing on squat.

---

## Programme Overview

| Phase | Weeks | Focus | Sessions/wk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 — Reconditioning & Symmetry | 1–3 | Tissue tolerance, single-leg control | 4 lift + 2 cardio |
| Mini-deload | 4 | Brief recovery, intensity held | 3 lift + 2 cardio |
| 2 — Volume Push | 5–7 | Strength base with high volume | 5 lift + 2 cardio (Sat combined) |
| Back-off week | 8 | Intensity held, volume cut 30% | 4 lift + 1 cardio |
| 3 — Intensification & Ski-specific | 9–11 | Heavy triples, ski-specific qualities | 4 lift + 2 cardio |
| 4 — Peak & Strong Day | 12 | Taper to performance test | 3 lift + 2 light cardio |

**Assumed example client:** 82 kg, 180 cm, 18% body fat, desk job. Calorie and macro numbers below are based on this; rerun with his actual stats.

---

# PHASE 1 — Reconditioning & Symmetry (Weeks 1–3)

## Weekly Split
- **Mon:** Lower bilateral
- **Tue:** Upper push + core
- **Wed:** Cardio
- **Thu:** Lower unilateral
- **Fri:** Upper pull + posterior
- **Sat:** Cardio
- **Sun:** Rest

## Lifting Sessions

### Mon — Lower bilateral
- Goblet box squat (parallel, knee ≤90°): 4 x 8
- Leg press (limited ROM): 3 x 10
- Romanian deadlift: 3 x 8
- Standing calf raise: 3 x 12
- TKE with band: 3 x 15 each
- Side plank: 3 x 30 sec each

### Tue — Upper push + core
- DB bench press: 4 x 8
- Standing DB OHP: 3 x 10
- Cable chest fly: 3 x 12
- Triceps rope pushdown: 3 x 12
- Dead bug: 3 x 10 each
- Pallof press: 3 x 10 each

### Thu — Lower unilateral
- Rear-foot elevated split squat (shallow): 3 x 8 each
- Step-up to low box (knee ≤90°): 3 x 8 each
- Single-leg leg press: 3 x 10 each
- Copenhagen plank (short lever): 3 x 20 sec each
- Hamstring curl: 3 x 12

### Fri — Upper pull + posterior
- Chest-supported row: 4 x 8
- Lat pulldown: 3 x 10
- Hip thrust: 4 x 10
- 45° back extension: 3 x 12
- Face pull: 3 x 15
- Suitcase carry: 3 x 30 sec each

## Cardio (Phase 1)
- **Wed:** 30 min easy bike OR 30 min swim (alternate weekly).
- **Sat:** Rower intervals — 6 x 400 m moderate-hard / 90 sec rest. Track splits.

## Week-by-week Loading

| Week | Lifting | Cardio Wed | Cardio Sat |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | RPE 6, tempo 3-1-1 on squats/split squats | 30 min | 6 x 400 m |
| 2 | +1 set leg press and RDL, RPE 6–7 | 35 min | 7 x 400 m |
| 3 | +2.5–5% loads, add 2-sec pause at bottom of split squat | 40 min | 8 x 400 m |

---

# WEEK 4 — Mini-deload

Three lifting sessions only, volume −20%, intensity held. One genuine recovery touch-point before the volume push.

### Mon — Lower bilateral
- Goblet box squat: 3 x 6
- Leg press: 3 x 8
- RDL: 3 x 6
- Calf raise: 2 x 12
- TKE: 2 x 15

### Tue — Upper push + core
- DB bench: 3 x 6
- OHP: 3 x 8
- Cable fly: 2 x 12
- Triceps: 2 x 12
- Dead bug: 2 x 10 each
- Pallof: 2 x 10 each

### Thu — Lower unilateral
- RFE split squat: 3 x 6 each
- Step-up: 2 x 8 each
- Single-leg leg press: 2 x 10 each
- Copenhagen plank: 2 x 20 sec each
- Hamstring curl: 2 x 12

**Cardio Week 4:** Wed 25 min easy bike. Sat 5 x 400 m easy rower.

**End of Week 4:** Assess knee, symmetry, soreness. Green light → Phase 2.

---

# PHASE 2 — Volume Push (Weeks 5–7)

## Weekly Split (now 5 lifting days)
- **Mon:** Lower bilateral (strength)
- **Tue:** Upper push
- **Wed:** Cardio
- **Thu:** Lower unilateral (strength)
- **Fri:** Upper pull + posterior
- **Sat:** Lower accessory + cardio
- **Sun:** Rest

## Lifting Sessions

### Mon — Lower bilateral (strength)
- Safety bar box squat to parallel: 6 x 5
- Trap bar deadlift (low handles): 5 x 5
- Leg press: 4 x 8
- Walking DB lunge (shallow, no impact step-down): 3 x 8 each
- Standing calf raise: 4 x 8
- Hanging knee raise: 3 x 10

### Tue — Upper push
- Barbell bench press: 6 x 5
- Standing OHP: 5 x 5
- Incline DB press: 4 x 8
- Close-grip bench: 3 x 8
- Cable triceps extension: 3 x 10
- Pallof press: 3 x 10 each

### Thu — Lower unilateral (strength)
- RFE split squat (DBs): 5 x 6 each
- Reverse lunge to low box: 4 x 8 each
- Single-leg RDL: 4 x 8 each
- Nordic hamstring eccentric (assisted): 4 x 5
- Copenhagen plank: 3 x 25 sec each

### Fri — Upper pull + posterior
- Weighted chin-up: 5 x 5
- Pendlay or chest-supported row: 5 x 6
- Hip thrust: 5 x 6
- 45° back extension (weighted): 4 x 10
- Face pull: 3 x 12
- Farmer carry: 3 x 40 m

### Sat — Lower accessory + cardio
Accessory block (RPE 7, no heavy compounds):
- Tempo leg press (3-1-1): 4 x 10
- Lateral step-up to low box: 3 x 10 each
- Seated hamstring curl: 4 x 12
- Single-leg calf raise: 3 x 12 each
- Standing cable hip abduction: 3 x 15 each

Then Format B sled & carry circuit, 4 rounds:
- Sled push 20 m / Sled drag backward 20 m / Farmer carry 40 m / Ski erg 250 m / Battle ropes 30 sec

## Cardio (Phase 2)
- **Wed:** Format C — Ski erg + assault bike intervals. 6 rounds of 90 sec ski erg / 90 sec bike / 90 sec rest.
- **Sat:** Built into the lower accessory day (Format B).

## Week-by-week Loading

| Week | Main lifts | Wed cardio | Sat circuit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | Establish loads, top sets RPE 7 | 6 rounds | 4 rounds |
| 6 | +2.5–5 kg all main lifts, RPE 8 | 7 rounds | 5 rounds |
| 7 | Peak week, top sets RPE 8.5–9, back-off double @ 90% on squat & bench | 8 rounds | 5 rounds + load |

---

# WEEK 8 — Back-off week (intensity held)

Volume −30%, loads heavy on top sets. Back to 4 days.

### Mon — Lower bilateral
- Safety bar box squat: 3 x 3 @ RPE 8
- Trap bar deadlift: 3 x 3 @ RPE 8
- Leg press: 2 x 8
- Calf raise: 2 x 10

### Tue — Upper push
- Bench press: 3 x 3 @ RPE 8
- OHP: 3 x 5
- Incline DB press: 2 x 8
- Pallof press: 2 x 10 each

### Thu — Lower unilateral
- RFE split squat: 3 x 5 each @ RPE 7
- Single-leg RDL: 3 x 6 each
- Copenhagen plank: 2 x 25 sec each

### Fri — Upper pull + posterior
- Weighted chin-up: 3 x 3 @ RPE 8
- Row: 3 x 6
- Hip thrust: 3 x 5 @ RPE 8
- Back extension: 2 x 10

**Cardio Week 8:** Wed only — Format C, 5 rounds, RPE 7. No Saturday session.

**End of Week 8:** Symmetry retest on single-leg leg press. Target <10% asymmetry. Green light → Phase 3.

---

# PHASE 3 — Intensification & Ski-specific (Weeks 9–11)

## Weekly Split
- **Mon:** Lower bilateral (intensification)
- **Tue:** Upper push (intensification)
- **Wed:** Cardio
- **Thu:** Lower unilateral + lateral
- **Fri:** Upper pull + posterior (intensification)
- **Sat:** Cardio
- **Sun:** Rest

## Lifting Sessions

### Mon — Lower bilateral (intensification)
- Safety bar box squat: see progression table
- Trap bar deadlift: see progression table
- Tempo leg press (3-1-1): 3 x 6
- Wall sit at ski angle (knees 100–110°): 4 x 30–60 sec
- Standing calf raise: 4 x 8
- Pallof iso-hold: 3 x 20 sec each

### Tue — Upper push (intensification)
- Bench press: see progression table
- Standing OHP: see progression table
- Incline DB press: 3 x 6
- Close-grip bench: 3 x 6
- Landmine press: 3 x 8 each
- Cable woodchop: 3 x 10 each

### Thu — Lower unilateral + lateral
- RFE split squat (tempo 3-1-1): 4 x 6 each
- Lateral step-up to low box: 3 x 8 each
- Skater squat (assisted, partial ROM): 3 x 6 each
- Single-leg RDL: 3 x 6 each
- Cable hip abduction (standing): 3 x 12 each
- Copenhagen plank (long lever if tolerated): 3 x 30 sec each

### Fri — Upper pull + posterior (intensification)
- Weighted chin-up: see progression table
- Barbell or chest-supported row: see progression table
- Hip thrust: see progression table
- Single-leg hip thrust: 3 x 8 each
- 45° back extension: 3 x 10
- Suitcase carry: 3 x 40 m each

## Main Lift Progression (Weeks 9–11)

| Week | Box squat | Trap bar DL | Bench | OHP | Chin-up | Row | Hip thrust |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **9** | 5 x 5 @ RPE 7.5 | 4 x 5 @ RPE 7.5 | 5 x 5 @ RPE 7.5 | 4 x 5 @ RPE 7.5 | 4 x 5 @ RPE 7.5 | 4 x 6 | 4 x 5 |
| **10** | 5 x 3 @ RPE 8 | 4 x 3 @ RPE 8 | 5 x 3 @ RPE 8 | 4 x 4 @ RPE 8 | 4 x 4 @ RPE 8 | 4 x 5 | 4 x 4 |
| **11** | 4 x 3 @ RPE 8.5, +1 x 2 @ RPE 9 | 3 x 3 @ RPE 8.5, +1 x 2 @ RPE 9 | 4 x 3 @ RPE 8.5, +1 x 2 @ RPE 9 | 3 x 3 @ RPE 8.5 | 3 x 3 @ RPE 8.5 | 3 x 5 | 3 x 4 |

## Cardio (Phase 3)

| Week | Wed | Sat |
|---|---|---|
| 9 | Format D — incline walk 6 x 3 min @ 12–15% / 2 min recovery | Format A — 5 x 4 min bike @ RPE 8–9 / 3 min easy |
| 10 | Format D — add 5–10 kg weighted vest, 6 rounds | Format A — 6 x 4 min bike |
| 11 | Format D — 7 rounds peak | Format A — 4 rounds (reduce, building into Week 12) |

---

# WEEK 12 — Peak & Strong Day

Three lifting sessions. Friday is the deliberate performance test.

### Mon — Primer session (light, sharp)
- Box squat: 3 x 2 @ 70% of Week 11 top double (fast reps, RPE 6)
- Bench press: 3 x 2 @ 70% (fast reps)
- Chin-up: 3 x 2 @ bodyweight or light load
- Hip thrust: 2 x 5 light
- Pallof press: 2 x 10 each

### Wed — Light movement
- 20 min easy bike
- 5 min mobility flow

### Fri — STRONG DAY
Thorough warm-up, build slowly through ascending sets.
- **Trap bar deadlift:** work up to heavy 3 @ RPE 8.5, then 1 x 3 @ 90%
- **Bench press:** work up to heavy 3 @ RPE 8.5, then 1 x 3 @ 90%
- **Weighted chin-up:** work up to heavy 3, then 1 x AMRAP at bodyweight
- **Single-leg leg press:** work up to heavy 5 each leg (symmetry test)
- **Wall sit at ski angle:** 1 x max time (final ski readiness test)

### Sat — Light flush
- 25 min easy bike or swim
- Mobility, foam roll

## Return-to-snow checklist
- Single-leg leg press symmetry <10% L vs R
- Wall sit at ski angle 60+ sec pain-free
- No effusion after lower sessions for 4 consecutive weeks
- Single-leg RDL clean with bodyweight + 20 kg

All green = cleared for snow.

---

# NUTRITION

## Targets (example 82 kg client)

**Maintenance:** ~2,650 kcal baseline. Adjusted by training day.

**Macros (g/kg/day):**
- Protein: 2.0 g/kg → 165 g
- Carbs: 4.5 g/kg → 370 g (baseline; flexes with training load)
- Fat: 0.7 g/kg → 60 g

## Daily Calorie Adjustments by Day Type

| Day type | kcal | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Lifting only (Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri) | ~2,650 | Baseline |
| Cardio only (Wed) | ~3,050 | +400 kcal as carbs |
| Lift + cardio combined (Sat, Phase 2) | ~3,150 | Protein 180 g, carbs 420 g |
| Rest (Sun) | ~2,300 | Drop carbs ~80 g |

**Phase 2 weekly average:** ~2,790 kcal. **Phase 3 weekly average:** ~2,720 kcal. Both sit at maintenance.

- **Lunch (~700 kcal):** 180 g chicken, 200 g cooked rice, large salad, 1 tbsp olive oil. 50P/85C/15F.
- **Pre-training (~300 kcal, 60–90 min out):** Greek yogurt 200 g, 50 g granola, berries. 25P/50C/5F.
- **Post-training dinner (~750 kcal):** 200 g salmon
